propositions: An AST gate must detect six categories of prohibited config/credential reads: ambient env read (os.environ subscript/get), helper-shim env read (KNOWN_ENV_HELPERS callee), load_config call, literal-getattr env equivalent, provider-credential read outside boundary, and backend-registry access below provider boundary.

The gate must reuse gen_env_registry.py's scan/KNOWN_ENV_HELPERS/matchers (single source) for env-read detection; receiver-object aliasing (src=os.environ; src.get(...)) must be resolved; shim-shaped callees absent from KNOWN_ENV_HELPERS and dynamic env reads fail closed as unresolved-env-read.

Owner sets must be derived at runtime from existing registries: composition roots own cats 1–4 reads (config.py, _config_sources.py, _child_env.py, anthropic_model.py, bedrock_model.py); provider-credential boundaries own cat-5 reads (enumerated runtime.py/access_check.py/settings.py/acli_subprocess.py under src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/); credential names from _child_env.owned_secret_names(), backend keys from static @register decorator scan (not import-time _REGISTRY), env baseline from gen_env_registry.scan + _deprecations.

A legacy-exception set enumerates current below-seam reads by exact path+symbol+rationale; the gate exits 0 on the current tree; a newly declared env name or credential lacking an owner triggers the drift self-test and fails the gate.

Callee and receiver aliasing must be resolved per module: direct calls, import aliases (from...import, import...as), local assignments (x=<callee>), and conditional receiver binding (src = os.environ if condition else env) all resolve to canonical forms.

Path-glob exceptions are structurally rejected; the gate exposes check(root)->list[str] and main(argv)->int, runs offline with no network dependency, is unit-tested with synthetic fixtures for each category in direct/import-aliased/local-aliased forms.
